title: Version 10 after version 9
hook: Text order and numeric order disagree about 9 and 10.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: that text sorting compares characters one at a time, so 'v10' can sort before 'v9', and padding to 'v09' fixes it

misconception: Files named v9 and v10 always sort in number order.
objective: Pad numeric version fields before lexicographic sorting.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: Text order and numeric order disagree about 9 and 10. Which names sort v9 before v10 alphabetically? Correct option: v09 and v10. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.

claims.text: The padded versions have the same width. This fixture demonstrates text sorting; many real file browsers already use natural numeric sorting.
claims.source: Derivation from the explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and transformations in src/lib/lifehacks/studyModels.ts; app documentation below provides command/filter context, not evidence of productivity gains or of every fixture-specific choice. Google Drive Help, Search for files in Google Drive, filtering and advanced search; retrieved 2026-10-13: https://support.google.com/drive/answer/2375114?hl=en . Exercise fixtures do not reproduce every Drive search behaviour. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): HELD UNVERIFIED. Fixture half holds: padded names v02, v09, v10 have equal width and text-sort into 2, 9, 10, while plain names text-sort as v10, v2, v9 (own node; GNU sort gives the same). The clause 'many real file browsers already use natural numeric sorting' is a claim about real file browsers. The only openable evidence on this host is GNU ls -v, which offers natural sort as an option, not by default; Drive Help 2375114 (the cited source) could not be opened. Left unverified. | FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Fixture half: padded v02, v09, v10 are all 3 characters and text-sort 2, 9, 10 (plain names sort v10, v2, v9). Real-world half, on opened sources (the cited Drive Help page could not be opened). GNOME Files (raw GitHub GNOME/nautilus src/nautilus-file.c) sorts names by g_utf8_collate_key_for_filename, which GLib documents (glib/gunicollate.c) as sorting 'file1 file5 file10'. KDE Dolphin (raw GitHub KDE/dolphin, dolphin_generalsettings.kcfg) has NaturalSorting as the default sort choice. Windows' shell API StrCmpLogicalW (MicrosoftDocs/sdk-api) compares digits 'as numerical content'. Builder: replace the Drive Help citation with these.

recall.question: A plain text sort lists draft1, draft10, draft2. Which names sort as 1, 2, 10?
recall.why: Text sort compares character by character, so '10' comes before '2'; padding to equal width fixes it.
